newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast late crudes rise, but diffs flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast late crudes rise, but diffs flat.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices gained with West Texas Intermediate (WTI), but thin dealing for Alaska crude turned even quieter late as traders attended an industry conference or waited for imports.
A three-day industry conference, hosted by Koch, continued to dry up activity late on Friday, but players were expected to return next week.
The discount for ANS remained $2.30 off November WTI.
No fixed deals occurred, with poor margins coming as NYMEX crude broke into new post-Gulf War levels of $25.85 a barrel Friday, ending 37 cents higher.
Tosco and Ultramar considered scaling back crude processing in early November to cut losses on weak margins.
Outright ANS prices extended early gains and ended 40 cents above Thursday at $23.35/23.65.
Traders said Arco might raise limits on shipments of crude oil across its California Line 63 next week.
"(Limits) could be a higher percent because margins are very weak and people may not be wanting as many barrels (shipped)," one trader said.
Line 63 crude remained prices at $3.20 to $3 off November WTI.
California heavy crudes remained flat. Kern River crude was $17.40/17.60 a barrel.
Values for Wilmington crude stayed $18.80/18.90 a barrel.
